result.title: FlyHash for LLM Agent Memory: An Empirical Validation and a New Application
result.comment: 19 pages. Code, data and interactive demo: https://github.com/mohanji/flyhash-agent-memory (archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23903302)
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on external memory stores to retain information across conversations, typically via dense vector embeddings searched with approximate nearest-neighbor methods. The fruit fly's olfactory circuit computes a locality-sensitive hash of sensory input using a strikingly different mechanism - sparse random projection followed by winner-take-all competition - and prior work (Dasgupta et al., 2017) showed this scheme, dubbed FlyHash, preserves neighbor structure better per bit than conventional random-hyperplane hashing (SimHash) on several benchmarks. We apply FlyHash, to our knowledge for the first time, to LLM agent memory retrieval, and ask three questions a practitioner actually needs answered: does the quality advantage hold under a correctly matched-bit protocol (it does, robustly, across 10 seeds and four datasets spanning two modalities, with one specific, previously undocumented comparison pitfall identified and corrected along the way); does that advantage translate into real memory and latency savings, including against the dense-vector indexing (HNSW) practitioners default to today (no: at equal bits FlyHash's codes are larger and slower to compare than SimHash's, and HNSW dominates both hash methods at ordinary scale; a sparse-set comparison we introduce recovers most but not all of a naive latency gap, leaving hashing's practical case narrower and more specific than the quality result alone implies); and does the advantage survive genuine, non-circular agent-memory relevance labels rather than the nearest-neighbor-by-embedding proxy this literature otherwise relies on (it does). We report all three answers precisely, including the two that narrow rather than flatter the headline result, and release our implementation, a working agent-memory demo, and a full account of the methodological pitfalls we found and corrected.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把果蝇嗅觉回路的 FlyHash（稀疏随机投影加 winner-take-all）用于 LLM agent 的外部记忆检索，在匹配比特数的协议下检验其邻域保持优势，并进一步比较延迟与内存开销、以及真实记忆相关性标签下的表现（结论显示实用收益远窄于质量结论）。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「稀疏投影 + WTA」哈希编码与比特级相似度成本核算，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据检索和 latent 相似度缓存、获取成本的设计提供核查线索；但任务面向文本 agent 记忆，与多模态推理状态的距离需较多判断。
